title: open_direct takes the agent twice, and a sync between the two makes a second room
description:
Store::open_direct (crates/mimid-agent-store/src/action.rs) looks for
the one-to-one room three times and holds the agent for only two of
them:

  1. Store::direct_room, over the records, no agent lock;
  2. Store::reveal_direct, which takes the agent lock and drops it;
  3. Store::host, which takes it again and hosts a new room.

Between 2 and 3 the lock is free, so a Store::sync can run. If that sync
joins a one-to-one room with the same user from a Welcome -- the other
side opening the same DM at the same moment -- then host goes on and
makes a second one. room-policy-04 section 5: "Only a single
fixed-membership room can exist for any unique set of participants", so
the hub refuses it, host leaves the room again and the user's first
PRIVMSG fails with a room already there.

It is also a second lock wait on the measured path. Bead mimid-604m.2
timed 1.09 s idle and 21.2 s under I/O pressure from the PRIVMSG to the
store_send span, of which store_host_room accounted for 429.7 ms; the
rest is the two acquisitions and the records read.

## The shape of the fix

Have Store::host take a &mut Agent rather than lock, and let its three
callers (create_room, start_call_with, open_direct) lock and pass it.
open_direct then reveals and hosts under one lock, which closes the
window and drops one acquisition. The critical section grows by
reveal_direct's reads, which are reads of state already in memory.

Left alone by bead mimid-604m.6, whose scope was the 28 write
transactions inside Agent::host_room.
